_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), Series Z1XYW/6 SET-2, Q.P. Code 31/6/2. 32 page images: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-30, Hindi on every odd index 3-29 (each the Hindi of the page after it); idx 31 is blank apart from the QR code and the 112 B box. Odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet: all Hindi, no English overflow. English numbering runs 1-39 unbroken across idx 4-30. Printed instructions confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ x1 (Q17-20 Assertion-Reason), B 21-26 x2, C 27-33 x3, D 34-36 x5, E 37-39 x4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 3-11, footer 086_31/6/2, this set only) for a bare OR: Q22, 26, 29, 32, 34, 35, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q22's OR sits between two unlabelled two-part blocks, so questionNumber is '22' / '22 OR' (as 31/6/1 Q25). All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page image (ms idx 2); each re-derived: all agree, Q2 and Q11 flagged as arguable. No void, grace note or dual key anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points on this paper are ORDINARY full stops (Q22 OR: 2.42 and 1.33). SIBLING of 31/6/1: 40 of 54 rows are the same questions, confirmed on this paper's pages and copied byte for byte from 31/6/1's file (stem, context, options, answer, chapter, subtopic, difficulty); figure notes written fresh from this paper's pages. Differences treated as typesetting and copied from the reference: Q17 Reason prints 'compoünds' with a stray diaeresis (as 31/6/1 does); Q39(c) prints the closing quote before the full stop ('for it”.') where 31/6/1 prints 'for it.”'; Q19 and Q20 print the Assertion with a hanging indent. 14 rows transcribed fresh: Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q13, Q18, Q21, Q24, Q29(a), Q29(b), Q31, Q33, Q34(a), Q34(b).

questions.stem:
(i) What are isomers ? Write the structures of two compounds having molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\) and give their names.

(ii) What are soaps ? How are they chemically different from detergents ? Why do soaps not work effectively in hard water ?

(i) What is a homologous series of carbon compounds ? Write general formula for alkynes. Name and draw the electron dot structure of first homologue of this series.

(ii) State the meaning of the functional group in an organic compound. Write the formula of the functional group present in alcohols and carboxylic acids.

questions.stem:
(i) What is meant by resistance of a conductor ? Define its SI unit.

(ii) List two factors on which the resistance of a rectangular conductor depends.

(iii) How will the resistance of a wire be affected if its

(1) length is doubled, and

Give justification for your answer.

In an electric circuit three bulbs of 100 W each are connected in series to a source. In another circuit set of three bulbs of the same wattage are connected in parallel to the same source.

(i) Will the bulb in the two circuits glow with the same brightness ? Justify your answer.

(ii) Now, let one bulb in both the circuits get fused. Will the rest of the bulbs continue to glow in each circuit ? Give reason for your answer.

questions._flag: Five one-mark reasons spread across the chapter: (a) DNA copying and variation (Reproduction and Variation), (b) pollination and fertilisation (Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants), (c) fragmentation and regeneration and (d) vegetative propagation (both Asexual Reproduction), (e) halving of chromosome number in gametes (NCERT's sexual-reproduction section). Filed on Asexual Reproduction, the only subtopic holding two parts.
questions.stem:
Give reason for the following :

(a) During reproduction inheritance of different proteins will lead to altered body designs.

(b) Fertilization cannot take place in flowers if pollination does not occur.

(c) All multicellular organisms cannot give rise to new individuals through fragmentation or regeneration.

(d) Vegetative propagation is practised for growing only some type of plants.

(e) The parents and off-springs of organisms reproducing sexually have the same number of chromosomes.

questions.context: All human chromosomes are not paired. Most human chromosomes have a maternal and a paternal copy, and we have 22 such pairs. But one pair called the sex chromosomes, is odd in not always being a perfect pair. Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes. But men have a mismatched pair in which one is normal sized while the other is a short one.
